newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes little changed after late rally.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes little changed after late rally.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed little changed as a late rally in CBOT soybeans sparked short covering by commercials and locals, floor sources said.
Prices had weakened earlier on nearby contracts on a combination of hedge selling, a strong Canadian dollar and an easier CBOT soybean oil market.
"The strong Canadian dollar is inhibiting export sales. We are too expensive at the moment," one WCE oilseed trader said.
Deferred contracts were mostly higher on crusher buying. Traders noted that crush margins on new crop canola were much more favorable than those for the current crop.
Flaxseed closed mostly higher on commercial buying with March bid up aggressively late and closing $1.50 higher at $358.20. Volume was moderate in both flaxseed and canola.
Feed wheat futures closed mixed. Dealers said strength in Oct and Dec contracts were due to MOC (market on close) buy orders in thin conditions.

Western barley remained little changed as the main feature continued to be rolling forward positions out of February into March, May and July. February barley closed steady at $137.50 while March wheat finished $0.70 lower at $170.80.
Feed peas were higher with UGG a featured buyer. May closed US$1.00 higher at US$197.00. Oats were thinly traded at mostly steady prices.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
